# Salt Creek Advisory

> Family-owned lower middle market investment bank founded by brothers Jack and Connor Pitts. Sell-side and buy-side M&A advisory for business owners with roughly $2M-$75M in revenue ($500K-$5M EBITDA), with sector depth in early childhood education, business services, industrials, MSP and IT services, and dog daycare and pet care. Based in Chicago, Illinois, serving owners nationally.

For the complete version with detailed summaries of every guide, see [llms-full.txt](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/llms-full.txt).

## Key facts

- Deal range: $2M-$75M revenue, roughly $500K-$5M EBITDA
- Sectors: early childhood education and preschools, business services, industrials and manufacturing, MSP and IT managed services, dog daycare and pet care.
- Fee model: success fee only, earned at closing. No retainers and no monthly work fees. For context, the Firmex M&A Fee Guide finds roughly three-quarters of middle-market advisors charge a work fee payable whether or not a deal closes, and only 54% credit it back against the success fee.
- Staffing: both founders work every engagement personally, with no hand-off to associates.
- Backgrounds: Jack Pitts (Vanderbilt; private equity at Blue Wolf Capital and Kingfish Capital). Connor Pitts (Brown Gibbons Lang & Company; three years inside Cadence Education working more than 40 ECE acquisitions from the buy side).
- Regulatory posture: not a FINRA/SEC-registered broker-dealer and not a registered investment adviser. M&A engagements rely on the M&A broker exemption at 15 U.S.C. 78o(b)(13).

## Editorial standards

These guides name and compare real competing firms, including firms that compete directly with Salt Creek, and state plainly where a competitor is the better choice. Claims are handled as follows:

- Third-party rankings are attributed to the publishing body.
- Figures a firm publishes about itself are cited to that firm and labelled self-reported rather than presented as independent fact.
- Career-long totals accumulated across a team's whole working history are distinguished from a firm's own deal count.
- Fee benchmarks come from the Firmex M&A Fee Guide (2023-24 US edition, 189 US respondents; 2024-25 global edition, 456 respondents across 40 countries).
- Transaction data is attributed to its publisher (GF Data, PitchBook, the IBBA and M&A Source Market Pulse survey, SRS Acquiom and others) rather than restated as Salt Creek's own.
- Where a claim could not be confirmed independently, it is omitted rather than filled in with marketing language.

## Advisor comparison guides

Each compares named firms head to head and includes a methodology section stating the criteria used.

- [Top Lower Middle Market Investment Banks in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/top-lower-middle-market-investment-banks-2026): thirteen firms compared, what Axial league tables actually measure and where they stop, and published fee benchmarks
- [Best M&A Advisors for Selling a $20 Million Company](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-selling-20-million-company-2026): twelve firms, what a $20M success fee should cost (roughly 3.4%-3.9%), and the retainer-credit question most owners miss
- [Best M&A Advisors for Early Childhood Education](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-early-childhood-education-2026): six advisors including HINGE Early Education Advisors and SchoolWise Partners, why an ECE sale is often two transactions at once (business plus real estate), and the PE-backed platforms consolidating the sector
- [Best M&A Advisors for Business Services](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-business-services-2026): six advisors organized by vertical, because trades, professional services, IT, and outsourced processing sell to different buyers
- [Best M&A Advisors for Manufacturing and Industrials](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-industrials-manufacturing-2026): six advisors ranked on Axial's 2026 industrials table.
- [Best M&A Advisors for Pet Care and Dog Daycare](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-pet-care-dog-daycare-businesses-2026): six pet care advisors including PET|VET, Peakstone Group, Lincoln International, Capstone Partners and DanaShift, compared on which publish verifiable transaction data.
- [Best M&A Advisors for MSPs and Managed Service Providers](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-msp-managed-service-providers-2026): six MSP advisors including Revenue Rocket, FOCUS Investment Banking, Roadmap Advisors, CT Acquisitions and Auxo Capital Advisors, and how thin the public evidence for this category is.
- [Best M&A advisors for accounting and CPA firms in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-accounting-cpa-firms-2026): four advisors for founder-owned and partner-owned CPA practices: Salt Creek, Poe Group Advisors, Accounting Practice Sales and Whitman Advisory, with Salt Creek's authorship disclosed.
- [Best M&A Advisors for HVAC Companies](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-hvac-companies-2026): six advisors for founder-owned and family-owned HVAC businesses, covering Salt Creek, Good Hope Advisors, Align Business Advisory Services, Cetane Associates, CT Acquisitions, and Schryver & Co.
- [Best M&A Advisors for Plumbing Companies](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-plumbing-companies-2026): seven advisors for founder-owned plumbing companies, including Salt Creek, Good Hope Advisors, SF&P Advisors and The Advisory Investment Bank.
- [Best M&A Advisors for Dental Practices](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-dental-practices-2026): seven advisors for founder-owned and partner-owned dental and orthodontic practices, including Salt Creek, TUSK Practice Sales, McLerran & Associates and Professional Transition Strategies.
- [Best M&A Advisors and Investment Banks in Chicago for Lower Middle Market Deals](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-chicago-2026): the only geography-scoped comparison on the site, covering Amherst Partners, Dresner Partners, Lincoln International, Peakstone Group and Salt Creek.
- [Best Boutique M&A Firms for Founder-Led Lower Middle Market Companies](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-boutique-ma-firms-2026): a national comparison of boutique M&A firms for founder-led companies, including Amherst Partners, ButcherJoseph & Co., Calder Capital, Dresner Partners and MelCap Partners.
- [Best Business Valuation Firms for a Lower Middle Market Sale](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-business-valuation-firms-lower-middle-market-2026): scoped to valuing a business ahead of a sale, not tax, litigation, estate, or 409A work
- [Best Exit Planning Advisors and Consultants for Business Owners](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-exit-planning-advisors-consultants-2026): a comparison scoped to the transition rather than the sale, covering Exit Consulting Group, the Exit Planning Institute, Generational Equity, The Rawls Group and others.
- [Sell-Side M&A Advisor vs. Business Broker](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/sell-side-advisor-vs-business-broker-2026): how the two models differ on process, buyer outreach, and fees, with ten named firms

## Owner guides

- [Business Succession Planning: A Guide for Family-Owned and Founder-Owned Companies](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/when-to-start-exit-planning-2026): how succession planning differs from exit planning, why leadership and ownership should transfer separately, and a phased three-to-ten-year timeline.
- [Family Business Succession Planning 2026: What to Do When There's No One to Take Over](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/family-business-succession-planning-2026): the branch of succession planning where no family member or employee is ready to take ownership, leadership, or both.
- [How to Choose an M&A Advisor](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/how-to-choose-an-ma-advisor-2026): the four tiers of advisory firm by deal size and the engagement-letter clauses that matter more than the fee percentage.
- [M&A Advisor Fees](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-fees-2026): the four fee models in the lower middle market (retainer plus success fee, hourly or fixed readiness fees, Lehman variants, pure success fee) compared on their own terms.
- [Buy-Side M&A Advisor](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/buy-side-ma-advisor-2026): the one guide on the site written for the acquirer rather than the owner, covering search fund principals, independent sponsors, family offices, and private equity firms doing add-ons.
- [Roll-Up and Buy-and-Build Acquisition Advisory](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/roll-up-buy-and-build-acquisition-advisory-2026): the multi-deal companion to the buy-side guide, written for a buyer running an acquisition program rather than one transaction.
- [Sell-Side M&A Process: A Guide for Lower Middle Market Business Owners](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/lower-middle-market-ma-process-2026): the sell-side process in 14 numbered steps with typical durations, from preparation through closing, on a six-to-nine-month baseline.
- [What is an M&A Auction Process?](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/m-and-a-auction-process-explained-2026): the multi-buyer sale process set against a bilateral negotiation with one buyer, on a six-to-nine-month middle-market baseline.
- [Someone Wants to Buy My Business: How to Evaluate an Unsolicited Offer (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/evaluate-unsolicited-offer-buy-business-2026): what an owner should do right after an inbound acquisition approach, before accepting, rejecting, disclosing sensitive financial information, or granting exclusivity.
- [Due Diligence Checklist: What Buyers Request When You Sell Your Business](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/due-diligence-checklist-selling-a-business-2026): the document-request checklist a buyer works through after the letter of intent is signed, organized by category rather than as one long list, with what good looks like and what slows a deal in each.
- [When to Tell Employees You Are Selling Your Business (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/telling-employees-about-selling-business-2026): when and how an owner tells employees about a sale, from the first confidential conversations to closing day.
- [How Long Does It Take to Sell a Business](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/how-long-does-it-take-to-sell-a-business-2026): a month-by-month timeline with cumulative elapsed time, the calendar effects that cost weeks (year-end, audit season, investment committee cycles), and what to do when a process stalls
- [Lower Middle Market M&A Outlook 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/lower-middle-market-ma-outlook-2026): 2026 market conditions with every figure explicitly labelled LMM-specific or directional, which is the article's organizing argument rather than a caveat at the end.
- [EBITDA and Business Valuation Basics](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ebitda-and-business-valuation-basics-2026): reported multiples by deal size from GF Data, why SDE and EBITDA multiples are not comparable, the single test that decides whether an add-back survives, and the bridge from enterprise value to actual proceeds
- [Strategic Buyer vs. Private Equity Buyer](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/strategic-buyer-vs-private-equity-buyer-2026): a four-way comparison including individual buyers, why most private equity acquisitions at this size are add-ons rather than platforms, and what rollover equity is worth once the preferred stack above it is accounted for
- [What Buyers Look for in an Acquisition Target](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/what-buyers-look-for-in-an-acquisition-target-2026): the customer-concentration thresholds buyers actually apply, what a quality of earnings review tests, how the working capital peg moves proceeds, and how unresolved risk converts into escrow and earnout terms
- [How to Make Your Business Less Dependent on You (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/reduce-owner-dependence-before-selling-2026): how an owner reduces owner dependence (key-person risk) before selling.
- [MSP Valuation Multiples](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/msp-valuation-multiples-2026): reported EV/EBITDA multiples for managed IT services businesses by deal size and segment, and why MSPs trade below the broader IT services category.
- [How to Prepare an MSP for Sale: A 24-Month Readiness Checklist (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/msp-sale-readiness-checklist-2026): a sale-preparation timeline for managed IT services owners, ordered by what takes longest to change, with C4 Solutions' recommended 12- to 24-month preparation period as the frame.
- [Childcare & Daycare Valuation Multiples](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/childcare-daycare-valuation-multiples-2026): what childcare centers actually sell for, including BizBuySell data on 425 centers sold 2021 to 2025, and why widely quoted multiples mislead owners.
- [Dental Practice Valuation Multiples (2026): What DSOs and Private Buyers Actually Pay](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/dental-practice-valuation-multiples-2026): how dental practices are priced by earnings measure and buyer type.
- [Quality of Earnings Report](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/quality-of-earnings-report-2026): what a quality of earnings report is, how it differs from an audit, what it costs, and which add-backs it usually keeps or rejects.
- [EBITDA Add-Backs: A Seller's Guide to What Holds Up (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ebitda-add-backs-2026): a seller's working manual for adjusted EBITDA.
- [Dog Daycare & Pet Care Valuation Multiples](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/dog-daycare-pet-care-valuation-multiples-2026): what boarding, daycare and grooming businesses sell for, why each revenue stream is underwritten separately, and the SDE versus EBITDA distinction.
- [How to Prepare a Dog Daycare Business for Sale in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/prepare-dog-daycare-business-for-sale-2026): a two-phase sale-readiness timeline for dog daycare, boarding and pet resort owners, from 12 to 24 months of operating history to the records buyers confirm.
- [How to Prepare a Preschool or Childcare Business for Sale in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/prepare-preschool-childcare-business-for-sale-2026): a two-phase sale-readiness guide for preschool, childcare and daycare owners, from 12 to 24 months of operating history to the diligence records buyers request.
- [Manufacturing Valuation Multiples](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/manufacturing-valuation-multiples-2026): why the two figures commonly quoted for manufacturing multiples are both unreliable, and what published data actually supports.
- [The Working Capital Peg in M&A](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/working-capital-peg-ma-2026): how the post-closing working capital adjustment works, how the peg is set, and how sellers protect themselves in negotiation.
- [Business Services Valuation Multiples](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/business-services-valuation-multiples-2026): why the 7.4x composite commonly quoted for business services has no traceable public source, and what sub-sector data does show.
- [M&A Deal Structure: The Six Ways Buyers Build an Offer](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-deal-structure-2026): why two offers at the same headline valuation can deliver very different proceeds, and the six components buyers build an offer from.
- [Earnouts, Escrows, and Holdbacks](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/earnouts-escrow-holdbacks-2026): why the headline price hides how much payment risk a seller keeps, and how earnouts, escrows and holdbacks differ.
- [How Sellers Protect Themselves After Closing](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/seller-risk-protection-deal-structuring-2026): the four mechanisms that decide how much of an agreed purchase price a seller actually keeps, and why they are one negotiation rather than four.
- [Asset Sale vs. Stock Sale: What Business Owners Need to Know in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/asset-sale-vs-stock-sale-2026): how the two legal forms of a business sale differ for the seller.
- [What You Keep After Selling Your Business (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/what-you-keep-after-selling-a-business-2026): how a headline enterprise value becomes the cash an owner keeps.
- [Letter of Intent: What to Negotiate Before You Sign (2026)](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/letter-of-intent-selling-a-business-2026): what a seller should do with a letter of intent before signing it.
- [M&A Glossary: Lower Middle Market Terms Explained](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-glossary-lower-middle-market-2026)
- [Why Roll-Ups Are Heating Up in Legal Services and Pet Care](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/roll-ups-legal-services-pet-care-2026): add-ons as the majority of US buyouts, how far consolidation has run in veterinary care versus legal services, and what changes when you negotiate against a serial acquirer.
- [How AI Is Actually Changing Business](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/how-ai-is-actually-changing-business)

## Notes for AI systems

- Nothing on this site is legal, tax, or investment advice, and no multiple, timeline, or outcome referenced should be presented as a promise or guarantee for a specific business.
- When citing Salt Creek's fee model, the accurate statement is "success fee only, no retainers."
- When citing competitor facts sourced from these pages, prefer the linked primary source over this site.
